t.3.39.1: Commanded as if by a king, the night-roamer Mārīca spoke harsh and contrary words to the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.3.39.2: By what evildoer, O night-wanderer, has this ruin been counselled to you, the ruin of you together with your sons, your kingdom and your ministers?
t.3.39.3: What evil-doer, O king, is not pleased with your being happy? Who has cunningly shown you this door to death?
t.3.39.4: Clearly, O night-wanderer, your enemies, feeble in valor, wish to see you perish, overpowered by one mightier than you.
t.3.39.5: By what mean-minded one, a speaker of harmful counsel, has this been advised to you, O night-wanderer, one who wishes to see you perish through your own deed?
t.3.39.6: Surely your ministers, O Rāvaṇa, who deserve death, are not being put to death, for they do not restrain you in every way when you have set out upon the wrong path.
t.3.39.7: For a king who acts from desire and has taken to an evil path must be restrained in every way by good ministers; yet you, who ought to be restrained, are not being restrained.
t.3.39.8: O best of victors, O night-wanderer, it is through the favour of their master that ministers attain dharma, wealth, pleasure and fame.
t.3.39.9: But when the opposite is the case, all that becomes futile, O Rāvaṇa; through the failings of the master, the other people meet with calamity.
t.3.39.10: For dharma and victory alike have the king as their root, O best of conquerors; therefore the lord of men must be protected in all circumstances.
t.3.39.11: A kingdom cannot be ruled by one who is harsh, O night-rover, nor by one who is perverse, nor by one who is undisciplined, O rākṣasa.
t.3.39.13: Many virtuous people in this world who have practised fitting righteousness have perished together with their retinues through the offence of others.
t.3.39.12: Ministers who give harsh and reckless counsel are surely ruined together with their king, just as chariots driven by inept charioteers are swiftly wrecked on rough ground.
t.3.39.14: O Rāvaṇa, subjects protected by a hostile and harsh master do not prosper, just as sheep do not thrive when guarded by a jackal.
t.3.39.15: O Rāvaṇa, all the rākṣasas will surely perish, whose king you are, harsh, evil-minded, and with senses unconquered.
t.3.39.16: This dreadful calamity has come upon you as suddenly as the palm fruit falling on the crow. What good is there in this, that you will perish together with your army?
t.3.39.17: But that Rāma, having slain me, will before long slay you. By this I have fulfilled my purpose, since I die slain by an enemy.
t.3.39.18: Know that I am slain by the mere sight of Rāma; and know that you yourself, along with your kinsmen, are slain once you have carried off Sītā.
t.3.39.19: If I am to bring Sītā away from the hermitage, with you joined together with me, then there will be neither you, nor I, nor Laṅkā, nor the rākṣasas.
t.3.39.20: Though I, who wish you well, try to restrain you, you do not accept these words, O night-wanderer. For men whose life is spent, who are as good as dead, do not heed the beneficial counsel spoken by their friends.
